existing_reusable_code: ggml/src/ggml-cuda/moe_stream.cu already contains Q8_0 CPU-compatible MXFP4 kernels and diagnostics guarded by GGML_MOE_STREAM_Q80_CPU_COMPAT / Q80_WRITE / hot-batch probe envs. The missing piece is not a scalar formula, but connecting a CPU-compatible Q8_0 src1 path to the down batch runtime without excessive host copy overhead.
finding: CPU fallback for GGML_TYPE_MXFP4 uses vec_dot_type GGML_TYPE_Q8_0 and ggml_vec_dot_mxfp4_q8_0, while moe_stream_batch down path calls ggml_cuda_moe_stream_mmvq_dev, which quantizes src1_f32 to Q8_1 and uses vec_dot_mxfp4_q8_1. This math mismatch explains nonzero local parity error and fixed-text top1 drift.
implications: Do not promote or benchmark Q8_1-based MXFP4 down writeback; correctness gate already failed.
A correct batch replacement must either consume the CPU fallback Q8_0 wdata or quantize src1 to Q8_0 with CPU-compatible rounding/scale before kernel launch.
The current batch API only receives src1_f32, so CPU caller/API changes are likely needed to pass src1_q8_0 row pointers/row_size into ggml_cuda_moe_stream_batch.
The existing Q80_WRITE path can provide correctness scaffolding but may not be fast enough because it stages Q8_0 rows per call; batch integration must avoid serial per-expert copies.
